owner_decision: 2026-11-10: the owner chose Mireclaw next and rejected the first concepts, a river gorge with the antlered beast in the water: Mireclaw should feel more swampy and less like a river, and the elk should not be in the water. The owner then chose concept D (a bog of still pools, reeds and hummocks, the beast on a dry island) and approved painting the full set into it. Later the same day the owner found the backdrop very streaky, with vertical lines all over, and chose candidate 1 of two repaints of the swamp floor. The owner then had the den cut so it stays behind the foreground tree.

generation.tool: imggen: OpenAI Images API, gpt-image-2.6-sunburst, masked edit, quality medium, complexity low

method: Each building is a masked edit of the empty swamp (image 1) with its box as the mask and a reference (image 2): a crop of the concept painting for the buildings the concept designed, a detail of it for style only, or the next stage's painting for earlier stages. Image 1 was a crop of the swamp around the box, scaled to the edit size, so the box filled about a third of it. The crop is centred on the box; where it ran past the frame, the swamp was mirrored at the edge for the edit, and the painting is the edit's part inside the frame, which crop records.

concept.note: Image 1 was the plot plan sketch (plan_sketch.png), image 2 the earlier Mireclaw town painting, used for style and building designs only.

revisions.change: The whole swamp floor repainted without its fine vertical hatching: the first backdrop drew the ground as thousands of thin upright reed strokes with upright reflections. One unmasked edit of the first backdrop (complexity high) that keeps the layout: the stump, the root mound, the island, the mere and the foreground tree. The buildings were painted on the first backdrop and are cut against it (painted_on); they are drawn over this one.
revisions.tool: imggen: OpenAI Images API, gpt-image-2.6-sunburst, edit, quality medium, complexity high

revisions.change: The swamp floor repainted with definition: the second backdrop had lost its hatching but left the ground soft and featureless, so the dark buildings did not stand out. One unmasked edit of the second backdrop that keeps the layout (forms moved by under 1 pixel): crisp hummocks, tussocks, mud and clean pool edges, lighter tops against dark water. The foreground tree and the top of the sky were blended back from the second backdrop through the keep mask, so the foreground mask still fits.
revisions.tool: imggen: OpenAI Images API, gpt-image-2.6-sunburst, edit without a mask, quality high, complexity high; white in the keep mask is blended back from the earlier backdrop with a 4-pixel feather

foreground.note: The great tree at the right edge stands in front of every building; the layers are cut away under it.

grounding: Painted into the empty swamp on its own plot by a masked edit; the layer is the building as BiRefNet marks it, with a short soft skirt of its painted foundation, and later stages keep the plot's ground line.
curation: Owner-approved dusk-fen set (2026-11-10); layers draw under the stage tint and light, clicks follow the building-only hit mask.

matting.input: 1024x1024, ImageNet mean and std, averaged with the mirrored window
matting.window: the building BiRefNet finds touching the plot in a first look (plot box and paint change over 70, margin 0.4), then margin 0.12, grown by 0.25 on a side the building covers over 0.02 of, at most 4 windows
matting.passes: a building with matte_passes is looked at that many times, each time with what was found (grown by 6 px) painted back to the empty backdrop, and its matte is the union

sources: The paintings, mattes, masks and reference crops are not tracked (art/*/source/**/*.png is ignored); they are in the source art archive (docs/source-material-storage-map.md) and come back with tools/restore_archived_source_material.py.
